clue.text: They are bound to hold different views, for instance

definitions.text: They are bound to hold different views, for instance

parts.words: They are bound to hold different views, for instance
parts.note: books of photographs or postcards are bound volumes holding many views, such as holiday snaps

explanation.surface: People committed to holding varied opinions, as an example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound' suggests obligation and 'views' opinions; really the things are bound books holding pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: Photo collections are kept in bound books that hold a variety of pictures or scenes.

clue.text: Hard to fathom why corruption engulfed good man and king

indicators.note: swallowed, so one piece is placed within the other

explanation.surface: Puzzling why scandal swallowed a saint and a monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corruption' reads as a reason for obscurity, but it is a synonym that wraps round the saint and king; 'why' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Obscure and difficult to understand, like deep matters one cannot plumb.

clue.text: Carries family headgear

explanation.surface: Wears the family's hat.
explanation.walkthrough: This tall fur cap is worn by British Guards regiments.
explanation.definitionFit: The tall black fur cap of Guards soldiers is an item of headwear.

clue.text: Encounter a group of hunters

definitions.meaning: a gathering of riders and hounds before a hunt

explanation.surface: Come across a hunting party.
explanation.definitionFit: To come across someone, and a gathering of foxhunters at the start of a hunt.

clue.text: A verse that's initially puzzling

parts.note: a poem whose first letters of each line spell out a hidden word, so its puzzle lies in its initials

explanation.surface: A poem that baffles the reader at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Initially' seems to mean 'at first'; it actually points to the line-initial letters that carry the poem's secret.
explanation.definitionFit: This form of poem hides a word in the opening letters of its lines, a puzzle in its initials.

clue.text: What an MP stands for

parts.note: an MP stands for election for a particular area, not what the letters abbreviate

explanation.surface: Asking what the letters MP abbreviate, or what principles a politician holds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stands for' suggests meaning or principle; really a British Member of Parliament stands as candidate for an electoral district.
explanation.definitionFit: A Member of Parliament is elected to represent a district, and runs for that seat.

clue.text: Orchestral piece initially written on back of envelope

indicators.note: at the start, so the opening letter of each following word is taken

explanation.surface: A musical composition first jotted down on an envelope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Orchestral piece' sounds like a composition; it is an instrument in the orchestra.
explanation.definitionFit: A double-reed woodwind instrument is one piece of an orchestra's line-up.

clue.text: Take things the wrong way and drunkenly hit girl

indicators.note: staggering about, so the letters of hit are jumbled

explanation.surface: Misunderstanding things and assaulting a woman while drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunkenly' turns HIT into THI.
explanation.definitionFit: To steal is to take things illegitimately, the idiom read literally.

clue.text: Firm takes on man well-spoken and persuasive

explanation.surface: A company hires an articulate, convincing man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' looks like an adjective but is a business.
explanation.definitionFit: A convincing, clearly argued case is one that is forceful and articulate.

clue.text: Influenced kid when speaking

indicators.note: said out loud, the word for the leather matches the answer

parts.note: kid is soft leather from young goats, and suede is a similar napped leather

explanation.surface: A child was persuaded while talking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kid' looks like a child but is the leather; 'when speaking' signals the sound-alike.
explanation.definitionFit: To be swayed is to be moved or persuaded by some force or argument.

clue.text: Willing to finish in debt

parts.note: the finish of something is its end
someone in debt is owing money

explanation.surface: Someone happy to end up owing money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Willing' reads as an adjective, eager; it is the verb, leaving something by will.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaving property to someone by will is bequeathing, or settling funds on them.

clue.text: There's possible danger back in this 80s form of gymnastics

indicators.note: a possible arrangement of the letters, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A warning that an acrobatic dance of the 1980s could hurt your spine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possible' rearranges DANGER BACK IN; the street dance, with spins on the back, boomed in the 1980s.
explanation.definitionFit: Acrobatic street dancing with spins and freezes is an athletic, gymnastic style of dance.

clue.text: Stood up for a lady

definitions.meaning: got to one's feet, past tense
a woman's name, also a flower given to a lady

explanation.surface: Got to one's feet in deference to a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Got up is the past of the verb to stand up; it is also a common girl's name.

clue.text: Sincerity, as a matter of fact

definitions.meaning: a phrase meaning in reality, as with 'in very deed'

explanation.surface: Honesty, and that is a fact.
explanation.definitionFit: Honesty equals veracity, and something that is factual is the real state of affairs.

clue.text: New star makes a comeback at Stratford

indicators.note: coming back means the word is read in the return direction

parts.note: a nova is a star that suddenly flares, once thought to be a new star

explanation.surface: A rising actor returns to perform at Stratford.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the river at Stratford-upon-Avon, Shakespeare's English home town; 'star' and 'comeback' suggest theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: The river flowing through Shakespeare's birthplace in Warwickshire is the one found there.

clue.text: Bustling atmosphere around the street

indicators.note: placed round, so one piece encloses the other

explanation.surface: A lively feel to the neighbourhood road.
explanation.definitionFit: Up and moving about, in a state of activity and stir.

clue.text: A case of a treacherous person entering the church

indicators.note: going into, so one piece sits inside the other

explanation.surface: An example of a traitor joining the church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A case of' reads as 'an instance of'; the case is a box.
explanation.definitionFit: A wooden box for packing goods is a type of container.

clue.text: Captains confused by mishap and stress

indicators.note: mixed up, so the letters of the two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: Ship commanders flustered by an accident and pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' shuffles the letters of MISHAP and STRESS together.
explanation.definitionFit: Commanders of vessels are captains, the officers in charge of merchant ships.

clue.text: Ham in a roll, it's said

definitions.text: Ham in a roll, it's said

parts.words: Ham in a roll, it's said
parts.note: a ham is an overacting performer; in a role, punned as roll, he overplays

explanation.surface: Describing a ham sandwich.
explanation.walkthrough: The sandwich is a pun: a ham performer in a role, 'roll' standing for 'role'.
explanation.definitionFit: A hammy performer overplays, giving a poor, exaggerated performance.

clue.text: Said sale is fixed and charged

indicators.note: fixed means rigged or rearranged, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A supposed sale was rigged and someone paid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is fixed' rearranges SAID SALE.
explanation.definitionFit: Attacked or rushed at, as troops charge an enemy.

clue.text: Rubbish played on violins

explanation.surface: Junk music performed by string players.
explanation.definitionFit: An old exclamation of dismissal, like nonsense, and also the bows used on fiddles.

clue.text: Clubs competing over three miles

definitions.meaning: an association of sports teams that play each other
an old measure of distance, about three miles

explanation.surface: Teams racing over a three-mile course.
explanation.definitionFit: A sporting competition of clubs, and an old unit of distance of roughly three miles.

clue.text: Having a meaning, but not having a purpose

parts.note: the drift of an argument is its meaning

explanation.surface: Something makes sense yet is aimless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having' is a link, joining the article to the meaning.
explanation.definitionFit: Lost and directionless, like a boat floating without control.

clue.text: The boy's in a whirl

definitions.meaning: a male given name, short for Edward

explanation.surface: A lad is in a state of confusion.
explanation.definitionFit: A boy's name, and a small circular current or whirlpool in water.

clue.text: Criticise the effect of a loose bearing

definitions.text: the effect of a loose bearing
definitions.meaning: a worn engine bearing makes a rattling noise

explanation.surface: Finding fault with the result of slack behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: To disparage someone, and the rapping sound a worn mechanical bearing makes.

clue.text: Sailor goes to and fro to see famous pop group

indicators.note: going one way then back, so the second time the word runs backwards

explanation.surface: A seaman travels back and forth to watch a celebrated band.
explanation.walkthrough: 'goes to and fro' means AB forward then the same reversed.
explanation.definitionFit: The Swedish band that won Eurovision in 1974 was a famous pop group.

clue.text: A unit in the Salvation Army East of Suez

indicators.note: placed within, so one piece goes inside the other

explanation.surface: A Salvation Army detachment posted east of the canal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'East of Suez' is an old British phrase for the lands beyond the Suez Canal.
explanation.definitionFit: The continent lying beyond the canal is broadly the region east of it.

clue.text: Say one is ready to move in agreement

indicators.note: spoken aloud, the word for ready to move matches the answer

parts.note: someone with bags ready is packed

explanation.surface: Suppose someone is prepared to act in agreement.
explanation.definitionFit: A formal treaty or deal between parties is a binding agreement.

clue.text: Profit declared — but disputed

explanation.surface: Earnings were announced but challenged.
explanation.definitionFit: To deny or contradict a statement, an old word for disputing it.

clue.text: Destructive youngster is sent back on vehicle

definitions.note: the answer is a noun used attributively, as in a vandal attack

indicators.note: sent back means the word is written in reverse

explanation.surface: A damaging teenager is returned home in a vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' places the reversed youngster after the vehicle in this across entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who wilfully damages property is destructive; the noun acts as an adjective here.

clue.text: Sergeant set out to part friends

indicators.note: laid out in a different order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An army NCO started off to split up companions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set out' rearranges SERGEANT.
explanation.definitionFit: To alienate people from one another is to cause close companions to part.

clue.text: Remained sober, we hear

indicators.note: heard aloud, the word for sober matches the answer

explanation.surface: Kept off the drink, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sober' seems to mean not drunk, but here it is serious and sedate.
explanation.definitionFit: Stopped on in one place or continued unchanged, past tense of stay.
